Subject: Finalizing post‑term excess charge amortization for Q1 invoice

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. Per our review of Aster Labs' Q1 activity, there is a supplemental charge for sustained capacity above the committed baseline in January and February. We've pulled a proposed path to close this without a lump sum payment: a three‑month amortization (Apr–Jun) that spreads the one‑time charge and credits back a small goodwill amount for the billing lag.

Attached: 20270301-AsterLabs-overrun-invoice.pdf (invoice showing the calculation).

Quick summary:
- One‑time overage amount: $48,750
- Proposed amortization: 3 months (Apr, May, Jun) — $16,250/mo
- Goodwill credit (billing lag): $2,000 applied to April settlement

As next steps: can you confirm Aster is comfortable with the amortization schedule and share the PO number the AP team will use? If you prefer, we can reissue an updated invoice that includes the amortization schedule and PO.

I'll hold off on posting the charge to your account until I hear back.

Best,
Lauren

Subject: Daily usage extract and amortization options

Samir / Lauren —

Per Samir's request, I've attached the daily consumption CSV that feeds the billing calculation (20270302-excess-breakdown.csv). The key spike window was 2027‑01‑18 through 2027‑01‑24 where a test cluster exceeded the baseline for sustained inference jobs.

Options for Aster (we modeled both):
A) 3‑month amortization (Apr–Jun): $16,250/mo; goodwill credit $2,000 in April; net Apr invoice $14,250
B) 6‑month amortization (Apr–Sep): $8,125/mo; goodwill credit $1,000 in April; net Apr invoice $7,125

Rationale: longer amortization reduces monthly cash impact but lowers goodwill offset. Both options assume no contract change — this is a one‑time post‑term charge. If you want us to convert into a committed capacity increase with a term extension to blend into ongoing committed spend, we can run forecasts and a separate commercial proposal.

I can produce an updated invoice with either option and include the daily CSV as a supporting document.

Attachments: 20270302-excess-breakdown.csv, 20270303-amortization-schedule.xlsx

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Revenue Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
